title: Choir and Sigil
premise: Marguerite Underhill, last of the oath-bound swordspeakers, smuggles goods and secrets through the Thornfell mountains while hiding from the order that betrayed her. When a stranger named Elias Vane stumbles through a rift mid-blizzard, she discovers his arrival was foretold a century ago in the Canticle of Ash — a book of prophecies naming tonight's date, her own name, and a covenant between the human realm and the winter-fae that was broken and buried. Hunted by the Hollow Choir, zealots who want the realms sealed apart forever, Marguerite and Elias must reforge the covenant at the Thornfell heartstone before the long winter finishes falling and swallows both worlds. In the end, Marguerite learns she is herself half of the old bargain — the swordspeaker forged as its living seal — and she must surrender her memories of Elias to complete it, choosing survival for two realms over the self she has only just begun to claim.
about_author: Hazel Joubert is a former choir singer and amateur cartographer who grew up in mountain towns where weather was treated as a neighbor with moods. She writes fantasy about people whose pasts arrive uninvited, usually in bad conditions.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She guides a contraband shipment through a hidden pass, demonstrating her uncanny knowledge of Thornfell's roads and hinting at an oath she no longer speaks aloud. A storm unlike any she has seen begins to fall. Emotional beat: competent solitude curdling into unease.

chapters.title: A Man Out of the Snow
chapters.summary: Still Marguerite's POV. Mid-blizzard, a rift opens and Elias Vane falls through, half-frozen, insisting he was walking home in spring. He carries a scrap of parchment bearing her name. She nearly leaves him; instead she saves him, hating herself for it. Beat: reluctant compassion.

chapters.title: What the Canticle Says
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Sheltering in a waystation chapel, he finds the Canticle of Ash, a century-old prophetic text describing tonight's date, the rift, and 'the Underhill woman.' His rational worldview cracks. Marguerite burns her copy; he memorizes his. Beat: vertigo of being written before existing.

chapters.title: The Hollow Choir Sings
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Zealots of the Hollow Choir attack the waystation, seeking to kill Elias before he can reach the heartstone. Marguerite draws her sword and speaks her first oath-word in years — and the mountain answers. Beat: terror and exhilaration of reclaimed power.

chapters.title: Roads Only She Knows
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating. Fleeing into the deep passes, they negotiate trust: Elias offers knowledge from the Canticle, Marguerite offers the roads. They learn the Choir has turned the mountain folk against them with lies about the coming winter. Beat: wary alliance forming.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A village under early snow has lost all memory of itself, its people smiling and hollow. The broken covenant, Elias realizes, doesn't just threaten winter — it is already eating memory. He watches Marguerite almost forget her own oath-name. Beat: dread made intimate.

chapters.title: Oath-Bound
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Flashback woven through present flight: how the swordspeakers' order broke the covenant a century ago to save themselves, and how Marguerite alone was bound as the seal and then abandoned. She confesses this to Elias by firelight. Beat: shame transformed into resolve.

chapters.title: The Choir's Offer
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Captured briefly by the Choir, Elias is offered a choice: return home through a controlled rift if he betrays Marguerite's route. He sees their leader, Prelate Sorrel, is a former swordspeaker who remembers everything the world forgot. Beat: temptation with a human face.

chapters.title: Escape on the Frozen River
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She rescues Elias in a night chase down a frozen river as the ice groans and splits. Elias chooses her side openly for the first time. The long winter visibly advances behind them like a tide. Beat: loyalty proven under pressure.

chapters.title: The Fae Still Sing
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Deep in Thornfell they find the winter-fae are not monsters but mourners, singing fragments of the broken covenant. One fae, Vess, recognizes Marguerite's sword and grieves over it. First proof the covenant can be reforged — and what it will cost. Beat: grief that clarifies purpose.

chapters.title: Half of a Bargain
chapters.summary: Vess's testimony, rendered through Elias's POV. The covenant required two keepers: a fae voice and a human swordspeaker bound as its living seal. Marguerite is not merely a survivor of the betrayal — she was made for it. She overhears. Beat: identity shattered and reassembled.

chapters.title: I Am Not a Door
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Furious and grieving, she tries to abandon the quest and simply survive the winter in the deep roads. Elias refuses to leave, arguing that survival without selfhood is the village's fate, not freedom. Beat: the theme's central argument, fought between friends.

chapters.title: Sorrel's Sermon
chapters.summary: Prelate Sorrel's POV (single chapter). She believes sealing the realms forever is mercy: no more stolen children, no more eaten memories, even if the price is the fae's slow death. Her sincerity makes her terrifying. Beat: antagonist humanized, stakes complicated.

chapters.title: The Heartstone Road
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Reconciled, she and Elias climb toward the heartstone as the long winter's edge overtakes them. The mountain tests them with illusions drawn from memory — Marguerite's dead order, Elias's ordinary life. Each must choose to walk past comfort. Beat: desire confronted.

chapters.title: What Elias Remembers
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. An illusion lets him live a full day of his old life. He wakes weeping, having understood he cannot go back even if the rift opens — the man who fell through the snow no longer exists. Beat: quiet, devastating acceptance.

chapters.title: The Choir Descends
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The Hollow Choir reaches the heartstone basin first and begins a counter-ritual to seal the rifts permanently. Vess arrives wounded; the fae mourners gather to sing against the Choir's hymn. Battle lines form around a stone that hums like a struck bell. Beat: convergence.

chapters.title: Hymn Against Hymn
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The battle at the heartstone: swordspeech against sermon, fae song against Choir chant. Sorrel duels Marguerite and nearly wins by attacking her doubts rather than her body. Elias breaks the Choir's ritual circle at terrible cost — a wound that will not close. Beat: climax begins.

chapters.title: The Price Named Aloud
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. With the ritual open, the covenant demands its keeper: Marguerite must bind herself to the heartstone and give up her memories — including Elias — to hold the realms together through the winter. Sorrel, seeing the true cost, falters. Beat: the bill comes due.

chapters.title: Covenant Reforged
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. As Marguerite speaks the binding, Elias does the forbidden thing: he steps into the circle and shares the burden, anchoring her memories with his own so she loses the past but not herself. The covenant takes both. Winter stops falling. Beat: sacrifice transmuted into partnership.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, fragmented. She wakes at the heartstone knowing her name but not the man holding her hand, while his memories of her surface slowly in hers like things rising through ice. Sorrel surrenders, undone by witnessing mercy cheaper than her seal. Beat: tender disorientation.

chapters.title: Learning Him Again
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Spring thaws the passes. Marguerite and Elias walk out of Thornfell together, reintroducing themselves day by day — stories retold, oaths rewritten rather than renewed. The fae sing a new verse of the Canticle with two names in it. Beat: love rebuilt from evidence.

chapters.title: The Open Road
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The final page mirrors the first: a shipment, a pass, a storm — but now she travels with a partner, and the mountains know her name and sing back. She writes her own line into the Canticle. Beat: hard-won peace, identity chosen rather than assigned.
